value_domain: MCS account phase code (P, B or A)
value_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.92
variable_description: Whether this super account has moved from saving into paying, reported by the fund rather than the member. The ATO defines the field as showing "whether a pension or income stream has commenced and/or has been paid from this account during the financial year", with P for a pension started or paid, B for a defined benefit fund that has paid a lump sum or rollover instead, and A where neither applies. It is the cleanest marker of retirement in the MCS, and PNSN_OR_BNFT_PMT_PHS_CMNCD_DT on the same row dates the change.
value_definition: A single character, P, B or A. B is only meaningful for members with a defined benefit interest, which BNFT_INTST_DFND_IND identifies.
limitation: Phase is judged on any year, not this one: the ATO instructs providers to decide "based upon benefits paid or pension commenced in any financial year, not only during the current financial year", so P persists once set and is not an event flag. The field also runs only from 2013, and for 2013 a code B from a fund without a defined benefit interest is treated by the ATO as an A, so early B values are not comparable.
rationale: The MCS specification defines the field, enumerates its three codes, states the different rules for members with and without a defined benefit interest and records the 2013 change in the meaning of B.
evidence_quote: Account phase - shows whether a pension or income stream has commenced and/or has been paid from this account during the financial year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Account phase' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so a reader would have taken P as a retirement event in the reported year.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator (Y or N)
value_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.90
variable_description: Whether this account could receive money rolled in from another fund, which decides whether the ATO could use it to consolidate a member's small balances. The ATO collects it so that "to determine a receiving account for the auto consolidation of low balance accounts a super fund will be required to report if a super account will accept rollovers", and adds that an account which will not accept rollovers "cannot be a 'receiving account'". It is an account capability reported by the fund, not a member choice.
value_definition: A single character, Y or N. The field is mandatory for the 2013 to 2018 statements and blank for earlier years, so it exists on six of the nineteen MCS tables.
limitation: It says what the account could take, not what it took. An account flagged Y with no inward rollover in the year looks identical to one that received several, and the MCS carries no rollover amount to tell them apart. A value of N also has several causes, from a pension account to a closed one, which this column does not distinguish.
rationale: The MCS specification defines the field, gives its two values, states the consolidation purpose it was collected for and records that it applies only from the 2013 financial year.
evidence_quote: To determine a receiving account for the auto consolidation of low balance accounts a super fund will be required to report if a super account will accept rollovers.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Inward rollovers accepted' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it read like a record of rollovers received rather than a statement of what the account was able to accept.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator (Y or N)
value_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.96
variable_description: Whether the member could ask to move this account's money out to another fund, which is the outward counterpart of ACPTD_INWRD_RLVRS_IND. A fund reports N only for the reasons the ATO lists, chiefly a non-account-based pension, an employer-sponsored defined benefit component, an unfunded public sector scheme, a risk-only account with no investment component, or a member with no interest left and a zero balance. Those five cases make the column a rough marker of unusual account types.
value_definition: A single character, Y or N, mandatory for the 2013 to 2018 statements and blank before that. Y means rollover requests would be considered; N means one of the listed regulatory or product reasons prevents it.
limitation: A Y does not mean the member asked to move, and an N does not mean they were refused, because the field is about whether a request could be considered at all. The five reasons for N are pooled into one character, so a defined benefit member and a member with a zero balance are indistinguishable here without BNFT_INTST_DFND_IND and SF_MBRSHP_ACNT_BAL_AMT.
rationale: The MCS specification defines the field, gives its two values and lists exactly the circumstances in which a provider may report N, which is what makes the column readable as an account type marker.
evidence_quote: N - no, rollover requests will not be considered because of a reason listed in regulation 6.30
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Rollover requests from the member accepted' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it did not say that N has a short closed list of causes or that the field is about eligibility rather than behaviour.

value_domain: Dollar amount, allocated surplus (MCS)
value_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.103
variable_description: Money moved to the member out of the fund's surplus, counted as a contribution for the old superannuation surcharge. The ATO defines it as "the amount allocated to the member from surplus on or after 1 July 1997 that exceeds an amount considered reasonable by an eligible actuary for super surcharge purposes", and only accumulated benefits providers report it. It is one of the four components that made up the pre-2008 total contributed amount, alongside employer accumulation, personal and other contributed amounts.
value_definition: A dollar amount reported by the fund for one member account for one financial year. Only the excess over the actuary's reasonable amount is reported, so it is not the whole allocation from reserves.
limitation: It is a surcharge-era field and it stops. The ATO requires it only from 1998 to 2005, makes it optional for 1997, 2006 and 2007, and zero-fills it after 2007, so the eight PLIDA tables that carry it end at 2006-07 and a zero in the later years means the field was retired rather than that no surplus was allocated. Allocations from reserves after that are reported at TFRD_FRM_RSRVS_ASSBL_AMT instead.
rationale: The MCS specification defines the field, restricts it to accumulated benefits providers, states the actuarial reasonableness test and gives the exact years for which it is mandatory, optional and zero-filled, which matches the eight tables in the registry.
evidence_quote: Allocated surplus amount - the amount allocated to the member from surplus on or after 1 July 1997 that exceeds an amount considered reasonable by an eligible actuary for super surcharge purposes.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Allocated surplus amount' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it did not say that only the excess over an actuarial threshold is reported or that the field was retired after 2007.

value_domain: Dollar amount, assessable foreign fund transfer (MCS)
value_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.114
variable_description: The part of money brought in from an overseas super fund that the Australian fund has to treat as its own assessable income. The ATO defines it as the amount included "in the assessable income under subsection 295-200(1) of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997" and explains that it "consists of the difference between what was transferred and what was vested in the member at the time of that transfer". It is the taxed slice of a transfer; NON_ASSBL_FORGN_FND_AMT holds the rest.
value_definition: A dollar amount for one member account in one financial year, in Australian dollars. It is a difference between two amounts rather than a gross transfer, so it is usually a small fraction of the money that moved.
limitation: It is not the size of the overseas transfer and cannot be used to measure one: the ATO's own worked example has $60,000 transferred with only $2,000 at this field. Amounts a member chooses to have taxed under subsection 295-200(2) are excluded here and appear only in CY_ALL_CNTRBTNS_AMT, so a member who made that choice can show a zero at this column.
rationale: The MCS specification defines the field by reference to the subsection that creates the liability, explains the difference calculation, excludes the member-choice amounts and gives a worked example with the amounts split across the three columns.
evidence_quote: Assessable foreign fund amount - any part of the amount transferred to the provider from a foreign super fund or scheme that the provider must include in the assessable income under subsection 295-200(1) of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Assessable foreign fund amount' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so a reader could easily have summed it as a measure of money brought in from overseas.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator (Y or N)
value_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.94
variable_description: Whether this account is a defined benefit interest, which changes how nearly every dollar column on the row should be read. The ATO defines the field as indicating "whether this statement provides information that relates to some or all of the member's defined benefit interest", pointing to section 292-175 of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 for 2013 and section 291-175 from 2014. Where it is Y, contributions arrive as an actuarial notional amount at EMPLR_NTNL_CNTRBTN_AMT rather than as cash at EMPLR_CNTRBTN_TOTL_AMT.
value_definition: A single character, Y or N, mandatory for the 2013 to 2018 statements and blank before that, so it covers six of the nineteen MCS tables.
limitation: It is a property of the statement, not of the member: a person can hold a defined benefit interest and an accumulation account and appear on two rows with different values, so counting Y rows overstates or understates the number of defined benefit members depending on how accounts are grouped. Before 2013 there is no flag at all, and the split has to be inferred from which contribution columns are populated.
rationale: The MCS specification defines the field, cites the legislative definition it relies on for each year and ties it to the separate reporting of notional and actual employer contributions, which is what makes the flag load-bearing.
evidence_quote: Defined benefit interest - indicates whether this statement provides information that relates to some or all of the member's defined benefit interest.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Defined benefit interest' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it did not say that the flag governs how the contribution columns on the same row should be interpreted.

value_domain: Dollar amount, CGT cap election, small business 15-year exemption (MCS)
value_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.109
variable_description: Money a business owner put into super from selling assets held fifteen years or more, and elected to keep outside the contributions caps. The ATO defines it as "the personal contributions which a member has elected to exclude from the contributions caps because of a CGT small business 15-year exemption". It counts against a lifetime cap shared with the retirement exemption column, which was $1,355,000 for 2015, so the two CGT columns should be read together.
value_definition: A dollar amount for one member account in one financial year. The fund reports it only where a valid Capital gains tax (CGT) cap election was received on or before the day the contribution was made; otherwise the money goes to PRSNL_CNTRBTN_TOTL_AMT.
limitation: It is a fund's record of an election, not a verified capital gain. The ATO tells providers they are "not required to investigate this issue", so a contribution can sit here on a member's say-so, and an election made after the contribution is invalid but may still have been reported. It also cannot be summed with the retirement exemption column as separate entitlements, because both draw on one lifetime cap.
rationale: The MCS specification defines the field, states the election requirement and its timing, sets out the provider's limited duty to verify, and gives the lifetime cap and a worked example of how the cap is consumed.
evidence_quote: CGT cap election amount for small business 15-year exemption amount - the personal contributions which a member has elected to exclude from the contributions caps because of a CGT small business 15-year exemption.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label wording with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it did not say that the amount rests on a self-made election the fund is not required to check.

value_domain: Dollar amount, CGT cap election, small business retirement exemption (MCS)
value_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.108
variable_description: Money a business owner put into super under the small business retirement exemption and elected to keep out of the non-concessional cap. The ATO defines it as "the personal contributions which a member has elected to exclude from the non-concessional contributions cap because of a CGT small business retirement exemption". Unlike the 15-year exemption column beside it, this one is truncated: anything above $500,000 in a year is invalid and must be reported as an ordinary personal contribution instead.
value_definition: A dollar amount for one member account in one financial year, capped at $500,000 by the reporting rule itself. The fund reports it only where a valid election was received on or before the contribution date.
limitation: The $500,000 ceiling means the column is censored rather than measured, so a large retirement exemption contribution shows here as exactly $500,000 with the remainder hidden inside PRSNL_CNTRBTN_TOTL_AMT. As with the 15-year column, the ATO does not require providers to investigate the validity of an election, so the amount records a claim rather than an entitlement.
rationale: The MCS specification defines the field, states the $500,000 invalidity rule and where the excess must be reported instead, and sets out the election and timing requirements.
evidence_quote: The provider must treat a member's election as invalid to the extent it is for more than $500,000 in a financial year. To do so, the amount of the contribution in excess of $500,000 must be reported at the Personal contributed amount field not at this field.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label wording with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it did not say that the column is censored at $500,000 with the excess moved to another column on the same row.

value_domain: Dollar amount, contributions to a previously non-complying fund (MCS)
value_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.118
variable_description: Contributions made while the fund was still non-complying, reported in the first year it became complying. The ATO defines it as "the amount of all contributions made on or after 10 May 2006 to the provider if it was a non-complying super fund but became a complying fund at the beginning of the financial year this MCS relates to", and contributions made after compliance go to the ordinary columns. It is a rare, one-off catch-up rather than an annual flow.
value_definition: A dollar amount for one member account, accumulating everything contributed since 10 May 2006 while the fund was non-complying, so it can span several years even though it appears once.
limitation: It is not a within-year contribution figure and must not be treated as one in a time series: the amount belongs to the years before the reported one. It also attaches to the fund's compliance history rather than to anything the member did, so a large value says the fund changed status, not that the person made a large contribution.
rationale: The MCS specification defines the field, fixes the 10 May 2006 start, restricts it to the fund's first complying year and directs later contributions elsewhere, which establishes both the multi-year accumulation and the one-off nature.
evidence_quote: Contributions made to a previously non-complying fund - the amount of all contributions made on or after 10 May 2006 to the provider if it was a non-complying super fund but became a complying fund at the beginning of the financial year this MCS relates to.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label wording with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned that the amount covers earlier years and would distort a year-by-year contribution series.

value_domain: Dollar amount, all contributions received in the year (MCS)
value_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.119
variable_description: Everything that went into the account this year, and the one column to use if you want a single total. The ATO requires the "total contributed amount received/credited for or otherwise attributed to the member's account for the relevant financial year before any taxes or expenses are debited", and states that it "must be equal to or greater than the sum of" the itemised contribution columns on the same row. The gap between this and that sum is the money with no column of its own, chiefly co-contributions and the low income super contribution.
value_definition: A gross dollar amount before contributions tax, fees and insurance premiums are taken out, reported before any reduction following a release authority. It is a superset of the itemised columns, not their sum.
limitation: Adding this column to the itemised ones double counts, because they are inside it. It is also gross of tax, so it overstates what reached the member's balance by the contributions tax the fund pays on the concessional part. It also excludes contributions returned within thirty days of the fund becoming aware they exceeded the cap, and contributions returned because the fund held no tax file number, which means a member who over-contributed and had it refunded shows a smaller figure than they actually paid in.
rationale: The MCS specification defines the field, states that it is reported before taxes and expenses, lists what it includes beyond the itemised fields, lists the exclusions and states the inequality it must satisfy against the other columns.
evidence_quote: This field must be equal to or greater than the sum of the following fields: Employer contributed amount, Personal contributed amount, CGT cap election amount for small business retirement exemption amount ...
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'All contributions received for the current year' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it did not warn that the column contains the other contribution columns and must not be added to them.

value_domain: Dollar amount, directed termination payment taxable component (MCS)
value_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.113
variable_description: The taxable part of a redundancy or termination payout that the employee directed into super instead of taking as cash. The ATO describes the arrangement as occurring "when an employer is directed by an employee/member to pay their termination entitlements into a super fund", and this column holds only the taxable component of such a transitional termination payment. It exists for the 2008 to 2012 statements alone, which is why it sits on five of the nineteen MCS tables.
value_definition: A dollar amount for one member account in one financial year, covering the taxable component only rather than the whole directed payment.
limitation: The concession ended on 30 June 2012, and from then the whole payment is an after-tax member contribution, so a zero in 2013 and later means the treatment was abolished rather than that no one was made redundant. Because only the taxable component was ever reported here, the column also understates the money actually directed into super in the years it does cover.
rationale: The MCS specification defines the field for the 2008 to 2012 years, states that the concessional treatment ceased on 30 June 2012 and directs later amounts to the personal contributed amount field, which matches the five tables in the registry.
evidence_quote: The concessional treatment of these amounts was a transitional measure that ceased on 30 June 2012. If an employer is directed by an employee/member to pay their termination entitlements into a super fund the entire payment is an after-tax member contribution paid by the employer on the member's behalf.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label wording with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it did not say that the column covers only five years or that later zeros reflect a repealed concession.

value_domain: Dollar amount, employer contributions to an accumulation interest (MCS, pre-2008)
value_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.100
variable_description: What the employer put into an accumulation account for the member, on the pre-2008 form of the statement. The ATO defines it as "the amount of contributions made by an employer on behalf of the member to an accumulation interest", and includes super guarantee, award and salary sacrifice contributions, super guarantee charge amounts the ATO forwarded, and the taxable part of super holding account transfers. From 2008 the equivalent column is EMPLR_CNTRBTN_TOTL_AMT, which is not defined identically.
value_definition: A dollar amount for one member account in one financial year, gross of contributions tax. It excludes anything the employer paid out of the member's take-home pay, which belongs at PRSNL_CNTRBTN_TOTL_AMT.
limitation: It stops after 2007: the ATO requires zero-filling once the financial year exceeds 2007, so the eight tables that carry it end at 2006-07 and a series joining it to the post-2008 employer column joins two differently defined fields. Because salary sacrifice sits inside it undifferentiated, it also cannot separate compulsory super guarantee from voluntary sacrificed pay.
rationale: The MCS specification defines the field, lists the four kinds of contribution it includes and states the years for which it is mandatory and zero-filled, which matches the eight tables in the registry.
evidence_quote: Employer contributed amount (accumulation) - the amount of contributions made by an employer on behalf of the member to an accumulation interest.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Employer contributed amount (accumulation)' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it did not say what the amount includes, that it ends in 2007, or that salary sacrifice is inside it.

value_domain: Dollar amount, employer contributions (MCS, 2008 onwards)
value_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.107
variable_description: Cash an employer actually paid into this account during the year, on the 2008 and later form of the statement. The ATO defines the field simply as "contributions made by an employer on behalf of the member" and lists super guarantee and award contributions, salary sacrifice, and super guarantee charge and super holding account amounts the ATO forwarded. From 2013 the ATO restricts it to "actual amounts contributed by employers", pushing defined benefit notional amounts out to EMPLR_NTNL_CNTRBTN_AMT.
value_definition: A dollar amount for one member account in one financial year, gross of the contributions tax the fund pays on it. It covers the eleven MCS tables from 2007-08 to 2017-18.
limitation: The field changes meaning in 2013. For 2008 to 2012 a defined benefit fund had to include notional taxed contributions here, and from 2013 it must not, so an employer contribution series spanning 2012 and 2013 will show a fall for defined benefit members that is a reporting change rather than a change in their super. Salary sacrifice is also inside the total, so it cannot be used as a measure of compulsory super guarantee.
rationale: The MCS specification defines the field, lists its inclusions and exclusions, and states both the additional requirement for defined benefit funds up to 2012 and the 2013 restriction to actual amounts.
evidence_quote: For the 2013 - 2018 financial years, the Employer contributed amount field is used only for actual amounts contributed by employers and, for defined benefits funds, should not include any notional amounts.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Employer contributed amounts' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it did not flag the 2013 change that makes a defined benefit member's employer contributions discontinuous.

value_domain: Dollar amount, employer contributions to a defined benefit interest (MCS, pre-2008)
value_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.101
variable_description: An actuary's estimate of what a defined benefit member's employer effectively contributed, used for the old superannuation surcharge. The ATO requires providers to report "that part of the total contributed amount which are surchargeable contributions for the financial year that constitute the actuarial value of the benefits that accrued to, and the value of the administration expenses and risk benefits provided in respect of, the member". No money changed hands in this amount; it is a calculated value, not a payment.
value_definition: A dollar amount for one member account in one financial year, worked out for 2000 to 2005 under the Superannuation Contributions Tax (Assessment and Collection) Regulations 1997 or another method the Commissioner approved in writing.
limitation: It is not comparable with the cash figures in the accumulation columns, because it bundles the actuarial cost of accrual with administration expenses and risk benefits. The surcharge ended for contributions after 30 June 2005 and no notional contribution had to be calculated for 2006 or 2007, so a zero in those two years means the calculation was not required rather than that nothing accrued.
rationale: The MCS specification defines the field, states what the actuarial value comprises, names the regulations used and records that the surcharge ceased for contributions made after 30 June 2005 with no reporting required for 2006 and 2007.
evidence_quote: Super surcharge does not apply to contributions made after 30 June 2005. As there was no requirement to calculate and report notional contributions for the 2006 and 2007 financial years provision of this data is not required for those years.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Employer contributed amount (defined benefit)' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so nothing said the amount is actuarial rather than paid, or that 2006 and 2007 are blank by design.

value_domain: Dollar amount, defined benefit contributions (MCS, 2013 onwards)
value_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.121
variable_description: The formula amount treated as this year's contribution for a defined benefit member, used to work out Division 293 tax on high income earners. The ATO defines it as "the amount of any defined benefit contributions, worked out using the formula specified in the Income Tax Assessment Regulations 1997 for the purposes of Division 293 tax". It is the uncapped twin of NTNL_TXD_CNTRBTNS_AMT: the ATO states it "must therefore be equal to or greater than the amount reported at the Notional taxed contributions field".
value_definition: A dollar amount for one member account in one financial year, calculated under regulations 293-115.05 to 293-115.20 rather than paid. Funded interests use the notional taxed contribution without the grandfathered cap; unfunded interests use the Schedule 1AA method.
limitation: The field is empty in its first year: the ATO calls it Notional employer contributions for 2013 and requires it to be zero-filled that year, so a defined benefit contributions series usefully starts at 2013-14 even though the column appears on six tables from 2012-13. A non-accruing member is also zero-filled, which is indistinguishable from a member the fund simply did not calculate.
rationale: The MCS specification defines the field, names the Division 293 regulations behind the formula, states the inequality against notional taxed contributions and records the 2013 name and the requirement to zero-fill it that year.
evidence_quote: Previously the defined benefit contributions field was called Notional employer contributions for MCS lodgments for the 2013 financial year. For the 2013 financial year this field must be zero-filled.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Defined benefits contributions' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it did not say the column is a Division 293 formula amount or that its first year is zero by instruction.

value_domain: Count of member records reported
value_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, sections 6.57 and 6.152
variable_description: How many member records the person has in this year's member contributions statements, which is a count of super accounts reported for them. It is the column that tells you whether a person's contributions have to be summed across several rows before they mean anything, since a member with three funds appears three times. It sits on the fifteen tables from 2003-04 onwards rather than on all nineteen.
value_definition: A small positive integer. The MCS specification requires a provider member account number and provider client identifier that together uniquely identify an account, so each counted record is one account with one provider, not one fund.
limitation: A record count is not an account count in the way a member would recognise: an amended statement is a separate lodgement, and an account opened and closed within the year still reports, so the number can exceed the accounts a person held at 30 June. The column is a derived count added for the asset and is not defined in the ATO specification, so this reading is inferred from the custodian's wording rather than published.
rationale: The ATO specification does not contain this field, which places it as a count derived when the statements were assembled for the asset. The specification does establish that a member record is one account with one provider, which is what the count must be counting.
evidence_quote: The Provider member account number together with the Provider client identifier must uniquely identify a member's account with the provider.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Number of member records reported' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it did not say that multiple rows per person are normal or that the count is derived rather than reported.

value_domain: Financial year (YYYY-YY)
value_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.53
variable_description: The Australian financial year the contributions on this row were made in, written as a span such as 2012-13. The ATO defines the reporting year as "the financial year within which the contributions being reported were made to the provider", which is when the money reached the fund rather than when it was allocated to the member. The same year appears as a single number in FIN_YR, so the two columns are two renderings of one value and one of them is redundant in a join.
value_definition: A seven-character span from 1999-00 to 2017-18, matching the nineteen tables in the asset. The ATO accepts MCS years from 1997 to 2018.
limitation: It is not the year the member is credited. The ATO tells providers to report a contribution in the year it reached the fund "even if the contributions are not allocated to the member until the following financial year", so a June contribution allocated in July belongs to the earlier year here and to the later year in the member's own account records.
rationale: The MCS specification defines the reporting year, gives the rule for when a contribution falls into it, states the valid range and gives worked examples of lodgements for earlier years.
evidence_quote: Financial year - the financial year within which the contributions being reported were made to the provider. Give the year in which the financial year ends.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Financial year (YYYY-YY)' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so nothing said that the year is when the fund received the money rather than when the member was credited.

value_domain: Financial year ending (YYYY)
value_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.53
variable_description: The single year the financial year ends in, so 2013 means the year to 30 June 2013. The ATO is explicit about the convention: "Give the year in which the financial year ends", and its example reports contributions made between 1 July 2011 and 30 June 2012 as 2012. This is the column to join on when matching MCS rows to income tax or payment data keyed by year ending.
value_definition: A four-digit year from 2000 to 2018 across the nineteen tables in the asset. It is the same value as FIN_YEAR rendered as one number, not a different period.
limitation: The end-year convention is the trap: reading 2013 as the 2013 calendar year, or as the year beginning July 2013, shifts every contribution twelve months. Joining it to a dataset that labels the same period by its starting year will silently pair the wrong years rather than fail.
rationale: The MCS specification states the end-year convention directly and gives a dated example, which is exactly the fact needed to join this column safely to other year-keyed sources.
evidence_quote: If information is being lodged in October 2012 for contributions made between 1 July 2011 to 30 June 2012, this field would be 2012.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Financial year (YYYY)' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it did not state which end of the financial year the number names.

value_domain: Insurance indicator (N or Y)
value_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.95
variable_description: Whether the account carries life, disability or income protection cover, which is how the MCS shows insurance held through super. The ATO collects it "to identify super accounts with an insurance interest", with Y meaning "an insurance interest is attributed to this account, or to the member in respect of this account". It is the column that explains a small account with premiums draining it, and it pairs with ACPTD_MBR_RLVR_RQST_IND, which flags risk-only accounts.
value_definition: A single character, N or Y, mandatory for the 2013 to 2018 statements and blank before that, so six of the nineteen tables carry it.
limitation: It gives no type, no sum insured and no premium, so a token default death cover and a full income protection policy look the same. Because a member with three accounts can be flagged Y on each, it also cannot be used to count insured people or to detect the duplicate cover the flag was collected to help find.
rationale: The MCS specification defines the field, states the purpose it was collected for, gives its two values and states the years it applies to.
evidence_quote: Insurance indicator - to identify super accounts with an insurance interest.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Insurance indicator' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it did not say what is being indicated or that the flag carries no amount.

value_domain: MCS amendment indicator (O or A)
value_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.89
variable_description: Whether this row is the fund's first statement for the member and year or a correction of one it already lodged. The ATO defines it as an "indicator to identify whether the MCS for a particular year contains original or amended data for a particular member", with O for a first lodgement and A where the member data for the year is being "lodged to correct errors or omissions in a report previously lodged in respect of the same member for the same financial year". Without filtering on it, a corrected member-year is counted twice.
value_definition: A single character, O or A, valid only for the 2008 and later statements and blank before that, so eleven of the nineteen tables carry it.
limitation: An amended row replaces the original rather than adding to it, so summing contributions across both O and A rows for one member-year overstates the total. The column also does not say when the correction was lodged or what changed, and it cannot flag an error nobody corrected, so an O row is not certified accurate.
rationale: The MCS specification defines the field, gives both codes with the conditions for each, and states the years for which the field is valid, which matches the eleven tables in the registry.
evidence_quote: Amendment indicator - indicator to identify whether the MCS for a particular year contains original or amended data for a particular member.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Amended MCS' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it did not warn that originals and amendments sit on separate rows for the same member and year.

value_domain: ASGS 2024 Local Government Area code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, July 2021 - June 2026, Local Government Areas
variable_description: The council area holding the residential address the super fund reported for the member. ABS builds these as "an ABS Mesh Block approximation of gazetted local government boundaries as defined by each state and territory", and its current release covers Australia with 567 of them. The vintage is 2024 while the mesh block and SA codes on the same row are 2021, because the council boundaries are re-approximated from those same 2021 blocks each year.
value_definition: A five-digit ASGS LGA code from the 2024 release, covering all of Australia including unincorporated areas and 19 non-spatial special purpose codes.
limitation: ABS states plainly that its "approximations of administrative boundaries do not match official legal boundaries and should only be used for statistical purposes", so the column cannot settle which council a member's property is rated by. It also describes the address the fund held, which for a super account is often years out of date, and members with an overseas address have no LGA at all.
rationale: The custodian labels the column only as an address variable; the ABS ASGS page defines local government areas, states the mesh block approximation, gives the count and carries the caution about legal boundaries.
evidence_quote: Local Government Areas are an ABS Mesh Block approximation of gazetted local government boundaries as defined by each state and territory.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Address variable' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it named neither the classification nor its vintage, and gave no warning against using it for a legal council boundary.

value_domain: Date of last contribution or rollover (DDMMYYYY)
value_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.91
variable_description: The last day anything went into this account, counting rollovers and transfers as well as contributions. The ATO uses it to decide whether the account is unclaimed money: "If this date is within the reported financial year, the amount payable to the member is not treated as unclaimed money." A date years before the reporting year is therefore the MCS's marker of a dormant account.
value_definition: A date written DDMMYYYY, mandatory for the 2013 to 2018 statements and zero-filled before that, so six of the nineteen tables carry it. The ATO forbids a future date.
limitation: It can be an estimate rather than an observation. Where the fund does not know, the ATO accepts "a reasonable estimate or default date" provided the unclaimed money conclusion is unaffected, and gives an example of a provider stamping every long-dormant member with one migration date, so clusters of identical dates across members of a fund are an administrative artefact rather than a real pattern.
rationale: The MCS specification defines the field, states the unclaimed money test that gives it meaning, permits estimated dates and gives a worked example of the default dating that produces spurious clustering.
evidence_quote: If the date is not known by the provider, then a reasonable estimate or default date is acceptable providing the treatment of unclaimed super money and consolidation for the member is unaffected.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Date of last contribution (DDMMYYYY)' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it did not say that rollovers count or that estimated default dates are permitted.

value_domain: ASGS 2021 Mesh Block code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, July 2021 - June 2026, Mesh Blocks
variable_description: The block of roughly 30 to 60 dwellings holding the member's residential address as the super fund reported it. ABS defines mesh blocks as "the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS" and publishes 368,286 of them, so this is the finest geography on a member contributions statement and the block the LGA, SA1 and SA2 codes on the row are built from. It appears on the fifteen tables from 2003-04, not on the four earliest.
value_definition: An eleven-digit ASGS Edition 3 mesh block code, including 114 non-spatial special purpose codes for people in transit or with no fixed address.
limitation: The address behind it is the one the fund holds for posting member statements, which members update far less often than they update it with the ATO, so the geography lags a person's actual home by more than the ATO client register does. Members with an overseas address are excluded from Australian geography entirely, and a mesh block is a land-use unit rather than a household.
rationale: The custodian labels the column only as an address variable; the ABS ASGS page defines mesh blocks, gives the count and design and identifies the special purpose codes that appear as valid values.
evidence_quote: Mesh Blocks are the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS and form the building blocks for the larger regions of the Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS).
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Address variable' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it named neither the classification nor whose address is being coded.

value_domain: Month of birth (01 to 12)
value_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.71
variable_description: The month the member was born, as the super fund holds it, with the day dropped before the file reached the asset. The ATO defines the field as "the member's month of birth (in MM format)" and instructs providers to zero fill it when the month is unknown. Age at a contribution therefore has to be built from this and MBR_IDV_CNCTNTD_BRTH_YEAR, which matters for the contribution rules that turn on age 18, 65 and 75.
value_definition: A two-character month from 01 to 12. Zero is a valid stored value meaning the fund did not know the month, not a January default.
limitation: A zero month is easily read as missing data of no consequence, but it removes the member from any age-at-event calculation that needs sub-annual precision. The value is also whatever the fund recorded, which need not agree with the birth month the ATO holds on the client register for the same person.
rationale: The MCS specification defines the field, gives its format and range and states the zero-fill rule for an unknown month, which is the fact that decides whether a zero should be treated as missing.
evidence_quote: Month of birth - the member's month of birth (in MM format) If the month of birth is unknown, this field should be zero filled.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Month of birth' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it did not say that zero is a permitted unknown code.

value_domain: Year of birth (CCYY)
value_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.72
variable_description: The year the member was born, as recorded by the super fund. The ATO defines it as "the member's year of birth (in CCYY format)" and validates it as "a valid value greater than 1890", with zero filling where the year is unknown. It is the workhorse age variable in the MCS, since it is present on all nineteen tables while the fund-reported death and phase fields are not.
value_definition: A four-digit year above 1890. Zero is a valid stored value meaning the fund did not know the year.
limitation: Year alone puts a member's age within a twelve-month band, which is too coarse for the contribution rules that switch on an exact birthday, such as the work test that once applied from 65. Because the year comes from the fund's own records rather than a verified source, the same person can carry different birth years across accounts with different providers.
rationale: The MCS specification defines the field, gives its format, states the validation rule and states the zero-fill rule for an unknown year.
evidence_quote: Year of birth - the member's year of birth (in CCYY format) If the year of birth is unknown, this field should be zero filled.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Year of birth' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it gave neither the validation floor nor the meaning of a zero.

value_domain: Member deceased indicator (N or Y)
value_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.78
variable_description: Whether the super fund has been told the member has died, which is a statement about the fund's knowledge rather than about the member. The ATO is precise about this: N means the "provider has not received notification of the member's death" and Y that it has. It governs the death date columns on the same row, since the ATO requires Y wherever a date of death is present.
value_definition: A single character, N or Y, present on all nineteen MCS tables.
limitation: It is a notification flag, so an N covers both living members and members whose death the fund has not heard about, and a fund can go on reporting a dead member as N for years. The MCS also records death primarily for co-contribution purposes, so it is not a substitute for the death registrations in the deaths collection, which are the authority.
rationale: The MCS specification defines the field in terms of notification received, gives its two values, requires Y where a date of death is present and states that the date is reported primarily for co-contribution purposes.
evidence_quote: Member deceased indicator - indicates if the provider has received notification that the member is deceased.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Member deceased' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it read as a fact about the person rather than as a record of what the fund had been told.

value_domain: Month of death (01 to 12)
value_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.87
variable_description: The month of the member's death as reported by the super fund, taken from the date of death field with the day removed. The ATO requires the date only where MBR_IDV_DCSD_IND is Y and requires it to be zero filled otherwise, so a zero here is the normal state for a living member rather than a gap. With MBR_IDV_DTH_YEAR it fixes the death to a month, which is what the co-contribution rules need.
value_definition: A two-character month from 01 to 12, or zero where the member is not reported as deceased. It is the month part of the single date of death field in the ATO specification, split for the asset.
limitation: A month on its own cannot separate a death near a 30 June boundary, which is exactly the case the ATO says matters: it requires an amended statement whenever the true date falls in a different financial year from the one reported. The value is also the fund's record, so it can be corrected, withdrawn or simply wrong, and the ATO provides for a member reported as dead who is not.
rationale: The MCS specification defines the single date of death field, its dependence on the deceased indicator, the zero-fill rule and the circumstances requiring an amendment, which is what this month column inherits.
evidence_quote: If the Member deceased indicator field is Y then this field should contain a valid date. If the Member deceased indicator field is N then this field should be zero filled.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Month member deceased' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it did not say that zero is the ordinary value for a living member.

value_domain: Year of death (CCYY)
value_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.87
variable_description: The year the super fund records the member as having died, split out of the fund's date of death field. It is the column that puts a death in a financial year, and the ATO treats getting that year right as the one case where an amendment is always required: "If the actual DOD is in a different financial year from the originally reported DOD, an amendment is always required once this is known to the fund." The ATO also requires the date to be later than the member's birth date.
value_definition: A four-digit year, or zero where the member is not reported as deceased. It is the year part of the single date of death field in the ATO specification.
limitation: It dates the death, not the reporting, so a death in one year can first appear on a statement lodged several years later and the account will look active in between. Because the MCS records death mainly for co-contribution purposes, funds have limited incentive to correct a year that does not change that outcome, and the deaths collection remains the authority.
rationale: The MCS specification defines the date of death field, states the amendment rule that turns on the financial year, and gives the validation against the member's birth date.
evidence_quote: If the actual DOD is in a different financial year from the originally reported DOD, an amendment is always required once this is known to the fund.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Year member deceased' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it did not say that the year can be reported late or that it is not the authoritative record of a death.

value_domain: Co-contribution acceptance indicator (A or R)
value_source: ATO, Member contributions statement (MCS) specification v10.1.3, section 6.88
variable_description: Whether the fund would take a government co-contribution or low income super contribution into this account. The ATO defines the field as indicating "whether the provider will accept a super co-contribution and LISC for this member", with A for accept and R for refuse, and sets three conditions: current membership, an account that is not a pension or income stream, and a tax file number held for the member. An A therefore doubles as evidence the fund holds the member's tax file number.
value_definition: A single character, A or R, on the fifteen tables from 2003-04 onwards. Where the value is A, the ATO requires an account balance to be reported, so an A row always carries a balance even if nil.
limitation: It says nothing about whether a co-contribution was paid or whether the member was eligible for one, only about whether this account could receive it. An R has three quite different causes pooled into one character, from a missing tax file number to a trust deed that declines the payments, and only the missing tax file number case tells you anything about the member.
rationale: The MCS specification defines the field, gives both codes, lists the three conditions for acceptance, notes that a provider may decline for its own reasons and ties an A value to the requirement to report an account balance.
evidence_quote: Provider can accept super co-contributions and low income super contributions for member account - indicates whether the provider will accept a super co-contribution and LISC for this member.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's two alternative labels with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it did not say that the value is about the account's eligibility to receive a payment rather than about a payment made.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the MCS non-assessable foreign fund amount question
value_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement 2013 and later financial years, Section E, question 52
variable_description: Money moved into the member's Australian super account from an overseas fund that the Australian fund does not have to pay tax on. The ATO asks the provider to report "any part of the amount transferred to the provider from a foreign super fund or scheme that the provider is not required to include in their assessable income", so the taxed slice of the very same transfer sits in the assessable foreign fund column beside it. The field also carries money brought across from a New Zealand KiwiSaver scheme under the Trans-Tasman portability arrangements. It is reported by the fund, not claimed by the member.
value_definition: A whole-dollar contribution amount for one member account in one financial year. It is the untaxed portion of a foreign super transfer plus any KiwiSaver amount, and it counts towards the member's non-concessional contributions cap.
limitation: It is not a measure of retirement wealth brought into Australia. Only money routed into a complying Australian super fund appears, so savings a migrant leaves offshore or takes as cash are invisible, and a zero can equally mean the fund treated the whole transfer as assessable.
rationale: The abbreviated name expands to the non-assessable foreign fund amount, a numbered question on the member contributions statement the fund lodges, and the ATO publishes instructions for that question in both the 2007-08 to 2011-12 and the 2013-and-later editions. The ATO site refuses some automated fetchers but serves the page to an ordinary browser request, which is how it was read.
evidence_quote: Provide any part of the amount transferred to the provider from a foreign super fund or scheme that the provider is not required to include in their assessable income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, 'Non-assessable foreign fund amount', with the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that the column is one half of a split foreign transfer.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the MCS notional taxed contributions question
value_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement 2013 and later financial years, Section E, question 44
variable_description: An actuary's estimate of what a year in a defined benefit scheme was worth to the member, standing in for an employer contribution never actually paid. The ATO requires the figure to be determined under the Income Tax Assessment Regulations and says it "will generally be equal to the notional taxed contributions as determined by the provider with advice from an actuary". A grandfathering rule caps it: for a member who held the defined benefit account on 5 September 2006, an actuarial figure above the concessional contributions cap must be reported as the cap. Funds have reported it from the 2012-13 year, which is why the column only appears on the later statements.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount for one defined benefit account in one financial year. It measures benefit value accrued rather than cash received, and it is reported separately from the employer contributed amount.
limitation: Grandfathering censors the top of the distribution, writing any figure above the concessional cap down to the cap, so the column understates accrual for exactly the high-value defined benefit members it matters most for. It also overlaps the defined benefit contributions field and must not be added to it.
rationale: The name expands to notional taxed contributions, a numbered question on the member contributions statement, and the ATO instruction for that question sets out how the amount is determined and how grandfathering caps it. The page is served to an ordinary browser request although the ATO blocks some automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: It will generally be equal to the notional taxed contributions as determined by the provider with advice from an actuary.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Notional taxed contributions' as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never explained that the amount is an actuarial construct or that it is capped by the grandfathering rule.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the pre-2007 MCS other contributed amount question
value_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 56
variable_description: Contributions into the member's account that fit none of the named categories on the statement used before July 2007. The ATO defines it purely by exclusion: an accumulation provider reports "all other amounts (apart from amounts regarded as reasonably attributable to interest) that are paid for, or by the member to the provider" that were not already reported at the employer, termination payment, allocated surplus and personal questions. Government super co-contributions were deliberately directed here rather than to the personal contribution question, because entitlement to the co-contribution was calculated from that question.
value_definition: A whole-dollar residual contribution amount for one member account in one financial year, being whatever is left after the named contribution questions on the pre-2007 statement have been filled in.
limitation: Because it is a residual, its content is not stable between funds: two funds with identical member experience can split the same dollars differently according to how they classified an amount. It also merges co-contributions paid by government with genuinely miscellaneous credits, so it cannot be read as private saving.
rationale: The pre-2007 tables carry the question set of the Superannuation member contributions statement in force before 1 July 2007, and the ATO publishes the completion instructions for that form as a downloadable guide, which defines question 56 by exclusion and states where co-contributions were to be reported.
evidence_quote: Superannuation (accumulated benefits) providers must report in this field all other amounts (apart from amounts regarded as reasonably attributable to interest) that are paid for, or by the member to the provider
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Other contributed amount' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said that the column is a residual whose meaning depends on how the other questions were filled.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the MCS other family and friend contributions question
value_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement 2013 and later financial years, Section E, question 50
variable_description: Super paid in for the member by somebody who is not the member, their employer, their spouse or the parent of a child under 18. The ATO calls it other third-party contributions and asks the fund to "provide the amount of contributions made for the member by relatives, friends and third parties", listing a permanently separated or former spouse, a parent of an adult child, another relative, a friend, an insurer paying contributions under a sickness policy and a government agency compensating an injured worker. A contribution from any of those people made in their capacity as the member's employer belongs in the employer column instead.
value_definition: A whole-dollar contribution amount for one member account in one financial year, covering third-party contributors and counting towards the member's non-concessional contributions cap.
limitation: It cannot identify who paid. A workers compensation insurer, an estranged spouse and a friend all land in one figure, so the column is not a measure of family transfers. When a couple separates permanently the same contributor moves out of the spouse and child column into this one, so a relationship breakdown looks like a change in contributor type.
rationale: The name expands to the other family and friend contributions amount, a numbered question on the member contributions statement, and the ATO instruction for it enumerates the contributors included and the routing rules against the neighbouring employer and spouse questions.
evidence_quote: Provide the amount of contributions made for the member by relatives, friends and third parties.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated 'Other family and friend contributions amount' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing distinguished it from the spouse and child column beside it.

value_domain: Date the account left the accumulation-only phase (DDMMYYYY)
value_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement 2013 and later financial years, Section D, question 38
variable_description: The day the member's account first stopped being purely an accumulation account and began paying a pension or a lump sum benefit. The ATO ties it to the account phase code on the same row: "provide the date on which the account phase first changed from code A to either code P or code B", and the field is left blank while the phase is still A. Providers may report "a reasonable estimate of the date" when the real date is not held, and the instructions give the example of a fund reporting an arbitrary 1 July 2003 for everyone whose pension predates a system migration.
value_definition: A calendar date written DDMMYYYY, present only on accounts that have left the accumulation-only phase. It marks the first change of phase ever recorded, not a change within the reported year.
limitation: It is not a retirement date. A transition-to-retirement pension started while the member keeps working sets it, and for a defined benefit member a single rollover or lump sum sets it as well. Because estimates are permitted, clusters of identical dates across many members are administrative artefacts rather than real events.
rationale: The name expands to the date the pension phase or benefit payment phase commenced, a numbered question in the member account details section of the statement, and the ATO instruction defines it against the account phase codes and permits estimation.
evidence_quote: A reasonable estimate of the date may be provided when accurate data is not held by the provider.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label with its date format and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said that the date is tied to the account phase code or that estimated dates are allowed.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the MCS personal contributed amount question
value_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 55
variable_description: Money the member put into their own super out of their own pocket, as reported by the fund rather than claimed by the member. The ATO asks providers to report "any personal contributed amount made by a person to an account in their name" and adds that these "may include deducted and undeducted member contributions", so the column mixes contributions later claimed as a tax deduction with straightforward after-tax saving. Entitlement to the government super co-contribution was worked out from this question, which is why the co-contribution itself had to be reported at the other contributed amount question instead.
value_definition: A whole-dollar contribution amount for one member account in one financial year, gross of contributions tax and of any later refund.
limitation: It does not separate deductible from after-tax personal contributions, so it cannot be used to identify who claimed a deduction. It is also per account, so a member with three funds has three rows and none of them is that person's total personal saving.
rationale: The name expands to the total personal contributed amount, a numbered question on the pre-2007 member contributions statement, and the ATO completion guide defines what the question covers and explains its role in the co-contribution calculation.
evidence_quote: Both superannuation (accumulated benefits) providers and superannuation (defined benefits) providers must report any personal contributed amount made by a person to an account in their name.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Personal contributed amount' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both the definition and the limitation, so it never said the figure mixes deductible and after-tax contributions or that it is one account among several.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the MCS personal injury election question
value_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement for 2007-08 to 2011-12 financial years, question 37
variable_description: Compensation money a member put into super after telling the fund to keep it outside the non-concessional contributions cap. The ATO asks the fund to "provide the amount of personal injury payments that a member contributed while notifying the provider that they were to be excluded from the non-concessional contribution cap", and confines the eligible sources to a structured settlement, a court order for a personal injury payment or a lump sum workers compensation payment. The member must have lodged the Contributions for personal injury form on or before the day of the contribution; where that fails, the same money is reported as an ordinary personal contribution.
value_definition: A whole-dollar contribution amount for one member account in one financial year, excluded from the non-concessional cap and populated only where the fund held a valid election form.
limitation: It is not a measure of injury or of compensation received. Most personal injury settlements never reach a super fund, and one that does without the election paperwork is invisible here because it is reported in the personal contribution column instead.
rationale: The name expands to the personal injury election amount, a numbered question on the member contributions statement, and the ATO instruction states what the amount is, which payment types qualify and what happens when the election requirements are not met.
evidence_quote: Provide the amount of personal injury payments that a member contributed while notifying the provider that they were to be excluded from the non-concessional contribution cap.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated 'Personal injury election amount' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained that the column records an election with strict paperwork rather than the fact of a payout.

value_domain: Date the provider stopped holding the member's contributions
value_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 74
variable_description: The day the fund stopped holding the member's contributions, reported only on rows where money left the account. The ATO's instruction is short: "Show the date the provider ceased to be the holder of the contributions". It belongs to the transfer-out block of the pre-2007 statement, which had to be completed for any contributions leaving through a lump sum, a pension, an annuity, a departing Australia superannuation payment or a death benefit. The block exists because the superannuation surcharge assessment had to follow the money to whoever was holding it, so the date is an administrative handover point rather than a member decision.
value_definition: A calendar date on the pre-2007 statement, populated only where the member row carries transfer-out information. Rows with no transfer out leave it empty.
limitation: It does not say where the money went or why, which the destination fields on the same row carry. Nor does it mark the end of a member's super: from 1998-99 a rollover to another fund was reported by the destination fund rather than through this block, so ordinary fund switching is largely absent.
rationale: The name expands to the date the provider ceased to be the holder of the contributions, a numbered question in the contributed amounts transfer-out section of the pre-2007 statement, and the ATO completion guide states both the instruction and the circumstances that trigger the section.
evidence_quote: Show the date the provider ceased to be the holder of the contributions (if you require any further assistance, see Superannuation Contributions Determination SCD 98/1).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's long label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the field belongs to a transfer-out block that is empty for most members.

value_domain: De-identified superannuation provider identifier
value_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement 2013 and later financial years, Section B: Provider details
variable_description: The super fund, approved deposit fund or retirement savings account that the member's account sits in, as a de-identified key. The ATO is careful about which entity is meant: the reporting obligation falls on the trustee, but the statement reports "the particular super fund, ADF or RSA that details are being reported for, rather than to the trustee or RSA provider with the obligation to report them". Grouping rows by this key therefore gives fund membership, and counting distinct keys for one member in one year gives the number of accounts that person holds. The provider type column classifies the same entity.
value_definition: An opaque scrambled identifier with no internal structure, one value per reporting provider. There is no finite list to publish: the domain is as large as the set of funds, approved deposit funds and retirement savings account providers that lodged a statement.
limitation: It is not a trustee and not a corporate group, so two products under one trustee count as two providers and a merged fund appears as a new key rather than as a continuation of the old one. On the later statement self-managed funds are absent, because they report member contributions on the SMSF annual return instead; the pre-2007 instructions still set a lodgment date for them, so the early years are not on the same footing.
rationale: The ATO defines precisely which entity a provider is on this form, which is what the identifier stands for, and lists the provider types that lodge it. The scrambling itself is a PLIDA treatment that ABS does not document, so the key cannot be resolved back to a named fund or an ABN and that part of the reading is inference rather than a published fact.
evidence_quote: the term 'provider' is used in this document to refer to the particular super fund, ADF or RSA that details are being reported for, rather than to the trustee or RSA provider with the obligation to report them
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Provider scrambled identifier' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what kind of entity the key stands for or what grouping by it buys a reader.

value_domain: MCS provider type code
value_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement 2013 and later financial years, Section B, question 14
variable_description: What kind of super provider lodged the statement: public offer fund, non-public offer fund, public sector scheme, retirement savings account and so on. The ATO publishes nine one-letter codes and instructs the provider to "use the appropriate code to classify the provider" and, "if more than one type applies, use the most specific type". P is a public offer fund, N a non-public offer fund limited to the staff of one employer or group, S a public sector scheme, X an exempt public sector scheme, D an approved deposit fund, E an eligible rollover fund, A a small APRA fund, C a constitutionally protected fund and R a retirement savings account. Self-managed funds are absent because they report on their own annual return.
value_definition: A single alphabetic code from the ATO provider type list, constant across every member row a given provider lodges for a year.
limitation: The most-specific rule means the codes are not the sectors an industry reader has in mind: a retail fund and an industry fund both report P, so this column cannot separate retail from industry from corporate funds. Its absence from the earlier tables is a change in the form, not a change in the fund population.
rationale: The name expands to provider type, a numbered question in the provider details section of the statement, and the ATO publishes the full code list with a short definition of each classification and the rule for choosing between them.
evidence_quote: If more than one type applies, use the most specific type.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Provider type' with no code list and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the page named a classification without saying what the classes are.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the pre-2007 MCS post-20 August 1996 ETP component question
value_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 53
variable_description: The part of an employer termination payment rolled into super that counted towards the superannuation surcharge. It is the output of a formula, not a payment: the ATO sets it as the post-20 August 1996 period of the employment divided by the total period of that employment, multiplied by the eligible termination payment. The question "only applies to rollovers made on or after 1 July 1997", and the surcharge it fed was abolished for contributions from 1 July 2005, so the column empties out in the later years even where redundancies continued.
value_definition: A whole-dollar apportioned amount for one member account in one financial year, forming one of the components of the total contributed amount rather than sitting outside it.
limitation: It is not the size of the termination payment. A long-serving worker whose employment was mostly before August 1996 shows a small figure on a large payout, so the column measures a taxable slice under a repealed regime rather than the generosity of a redundancy.
rationale: The name expands to the post-20 August 1996 component of an employer eligible termination payment, a numbered question on the pre-2007 statement, and the ATO completion guide gives the apportionment formula and the rollover date restriction.
evidence_quote: This question only applies to rollovers made on or after 1 July 1997.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label, complete with its typo, and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the figure is an apportionment formula tied to a surcharge that no longer exists.

value_domain: ASGS Edition 3 Statistical Area Level 1 code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 1
variable_description: The small area the member's residential address falls in, at the finest level ABS routinely publishes. ABS designs an SA1 around a few hundred people: "SA1s generally have a population of 200 to 800 people, and an average population of about 400 people", and there are 61,845 of them covering Australia without gaps. The address behind it is the one the super fund held for the member, which the fund is required to report where it has one. The SA2, LGA and state columns on the same row are the same address at coarser resolution.
value_definition: An eleven-digit fully hierarchical ASGS Edition 3 code made up of the one-digit state or territory identifier and the Statistical Area Level 1 to 4 identifiers. Thirty-four non-spatial special purpose codes cover populations such as no usual address and migratory.
limitation: A fund's address is a mailing address kept current only as well as the member keeps the fund informed, so a member who moved and did not tell the fund stays in the wrong SA1 for years. Every year of the statement is coded to the 2021 boundaries, so an early record is placed in an area that did not exist in that form at the time.
rationale: The custodian's description says only 'Address variable', and the column name gives the classification and its edition. ABS publishes what an SA1 is, how many there are, the design population and the structure of the code, which is what a reader needs to know whether the column can carry a small-area analysis.
evidence_quote: SA1s generally have a population of 200 to 800 people, and an average population of about 400 people.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Address variable' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the definition and the limitation, so the page did not even name the geography, let alone its resolution.

value_domain: ASGS Edition 3 Statistical Area Level 2 code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 2
variable_description: The suburb-scale area for the member's address, and the level at which fund membership can be compared with a published population. ABS says "SA2s are generally the smallest areas used for the release of ABS non-Census of Population and Housing statistics, including Estimated Resident Population", so this is the finest column on the row with a ready denominator. In large urban areas an SA2 is named for the gazetted suburbs it contains, and in rural areas for the locality or town it is associated with. The SA1 column beside it is a finer cut of the same address.
value_definition: A nine-digit fully hierarchical ASGS Edition 3 code made up of the one-digit state or territory identifier and the Statistical Area Level 2 to 4 identifiers, where the SA2 part is a four-digit code assigned alphabetically within an SA3.
limitation: An SA2 built for a few thousand people is a poor unit in remote Australia, where ABS itself notes that an area of that population may be too large and diverse to be meaningful. The column also cannot be joined to the older five-digit short codes, which Edition 3 withdrew.
