rationale: The custodian's description is only 'Address variable', and the column name gives the classification and edition. ABS publishes what an SA2 is for, how it is coded and where it works badly, which decides whether this is the right column for area analysis.
evidence_quote: SA2s are generally the smallest areas used for the release of ABS non-Census of Population and Housing statistics, including Estimated Resident Population and Health and Vitals data.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Address variable' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it neither named the geography nor said what makes SA2 the useful level.

value_domain: Member account balance as a withdrawal benefit (dollars)
value_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 58
variable_description: How much the member could have taken out of the account, rather than what the account was worth on 30 June. The ATO asks the fund to "show the member's withdrawal benefit as at the last member reporting date", which for most funds is the 30 June annual statement, and the later editions of the form accept the most recent figure the fund holds when it lodges. The field had to be supplied where the fund could accept government co-contributions for the member, so how completely it is filled follows co-contribution eligibility rather than account size.
value_definition: A whole-dollar balance for one member account, measured as the amount payable on withdrawal at the fund's own reporting date rather than at a date common to all funds.
limitation: Balances are not comparable across funds on a single date, and for a defined benefit interest a withdrawal benefit can differ sharply from the value of the pension actually promised. Summing a person's rows gives a total only where every fund they belong to reported.
rationale: The name expands to the super fund membership account balance amount, a numbered question on the member contributions statement, and both the pre-2007 guide and the 2007-08 to 2011-12 instructions define it as the withdrawal benefit at the fund's own reporting date.
evidence_quote: Show the member's withdrawal benefit as at the last member reporting date - for example, the 30 June annual statement to the member.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Account balance' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing warned that the figure is a withdrawal benefit at a fund-chosen date rather than a 30 June balance.

value_domain: Date contributions first went into the account (DDMMYYYY)
value_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement for 2007-08 to 2011-12 financial years, question 32
variable_description: The day contributions first started going into this account with this fund, which is not the day the member joined. The ATO defines it as "the date that contributions began to be paid into, or otherwise attributed or credited to, the member's account with the provider". Two dump codes are written into the rules: an unknown opening before 7 May 1997 is reported as 1 January 1900, and one between 7 May 1997 and 1 July 2007 as 30 June 2007. Those two dates therefore carry a large share of the mass and mean not known rather than opened then.
value_definition: A calendar date written DDMMYYYY for one member account, marking the start of contributions to that account with that provider.
limitation: It cannot date the start of a working life or of super membership. A member who consolidates decades of savings into a new fund gets a fresh opening date, so account tenure built from this column understates how long the person has been in the system.
rationale: The name expands to the date the super fund membership account was opened, a numbered question in the member account details section, and the ATO instruction gives both the definition and the two substitute dates to be used when the real date is unknown.
evidence_quote: Provide the date that contributions began to be paid into, or otherwise attributed or credited to, the member's account with the provider.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Date account opened' with its format and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned about the two substitute dates that dominate the early distribution.

value_domain: MCS account status code
value_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement 2013 and later financial years, Section D, question 36
variable_description: Whether the account could still take contributions, in the fund's own judgement. The pre-2007 form offered two states, active or closed; from 2013 the ATO replaced them with three codes, O for open and not lost, L for open where the member is a lost member, and C for closed, which "includes those in pension phase". An account paying a pension is therefore reported as closed even though it holds money, which is the trap in reading the column as whether an account exists. An insurance-only account, by contrast, is reported as open.
value_definition: A short code for one member account in one financial year: active or closed on the earlier statement, and O, L or C from the 2013 form onwards.
limitation: Closed does not mean empty and open does not mean contributed to. The code tracks whether ATO payments can be accepted, so a large pension account reads as closed while a dormant insurance-only account reads as open, and the two vocabularies either side of 2013 are not the same variable.
rationale: The name expands to the super fund membership account status code, a numbered question in the member account details section, and the ATO publishes the code table with worked examples of which accounts are open and which are closed. The custodian's own label already shows the two vocabularies mixed together.
evidence_quote: The member's account is closed (this includes those in pension phase) and will not accept payments from us.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's mixed label, 'Account status: Active/Open and not lost/closed', with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it neither listed the codes nor flagged that the vocabulary changed in 2013.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the MCS spouse and child contributions question
value_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement for 2007-08 to 2011-12 financial years, question 38
variable_description: Super paid in for the member by their spouse, or paid in for a member who is a child under 18, reported as a single figure. The ATO asks the fund to "provide the contributions made for a member by their spouse or made for a member who is a child under 18 years old" and excludes a spouse who is also the member's employer, whose contributions belong in the employer column. From the 2010 statement the definition of spouse widened to include registered relationships and de facto partners of the same or a different sex, so the series is not continuous across 1 July 2009.
value_definition: A whole-dollar contribution amount for one member account in one financial year, combining spouse contributions and contributions for a child under 18 without distinguishing them.
limitation: The two components cannot be separated, so a rise could be either spouse contributions or contributions for children. The widened definition of spouse from 2010 adds contributors without any change in behaviour, which makes a break in the series look like a trend.
rationale: The name expands to spouse and child contributions amount, a numbered question on the member contributions statement, and the ATO instruction gives the inclusions, the exclusions that route contributions to neighbouring columns, and the date the definition of spouse changed.
evidence_quote: Only apply the changed definition of spouse to MCSs lodged for the 2010 and later financial years.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated 'Spouse and child contributions amount' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the two components are merged or that the definition of spouse changed mid-series.

value_domain: ASGS state and territory identifier
value_source: ABS, Census geography glossary, Australia (AUS) and State/Territory (S/T)
variable_description: The state or territory of the member's address, at the top of the ABS geographic hierarchy. ABS recognises the eight states and territories plus a ninth category, since "Jervis Bay Territory, and the Territories of Christmas Island, Cocos (Keeling) Islands and Norfolk Island are included as one spatial unit at the S/T level under the category of Other Territories". The identifier is the leading digit of the SA1 and SA2 codes on the same row, so the three geography columns cannot disagree with one another.
value_definition: A one-digit ASGS state and territory identifier, the highest level of the hierarchy that also produces the SA1 and SA2 codes on the row.
limitation: It is the state the fund had an address in, not the state the member worked or paid tax in, and cross-border commuting is common enough for the two to differ. An overseas or missing address has no identifier at all rather than a code meaning overseas.
rationale: The custodian's description says only 'Address variable', and the column name gives the classification and its vintage. The ABS geography glossary states which units the state and territory level recognises, including the pooling of the external territories, which is the fact a user coding to eight states would otherwise miss.
evidence_quote: Jervis Bay Territory, and the Territories of Christmas Island, Cocos (Keeling) Islands and Norfolk Island are included as one spatial unit at the S/T level under the category of Other Territories.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Address variable' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it neither named the classification nor mentioned the Other Territories category.

value_domain: MCS supplier-to-provider relationship code
value_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement 2013 and later financial years, Section B, question 11
variable_description: Who prepared and lodged the statement on the fund's behalf, as a one-letter relationship code. The ATO separates self-administration from the kinds of firm that run other people's funds: A means "there is no supplier and the provider is acting on its own behalf in the lodgment of this MCS", while C is an accountancy practice, F a financial planning practice, I an industry administrator, R a retail administrator, S a specialist firm, consultancy or life insurance office, T a tax agent, U an actuarial administrator, L a liquidator, W a controller or administrator and X the trustee of a bankrupt estate. Where the supplier is neither the provider nor its administrator, the field is left blank.
value_definition: A single alphabetic code describing the lodging party's relationship to the reporting provider, constant across every member row in one lodgment.
limitation: It describes the administrator, not the fund, so an industry fund that outsources administration to a retail administrator reports R. The blank is not a residual category: the ATO's rule makes the code inapplicable in a defined case, so blanks cannot be pooled with any code as an other group.
rationale: The name expands to the supplier's relationship with the provider, a numbered question in the provider details section of the statement, and the ATO publishes the full code list along with the rule for leaving it blank. The same list appears in the pre-2007 and the 2007-08 to 2011-12 editions of the form.
evidence_quote: If the supplier is neither the provider's administrator nor the provider itself, leave this code blank.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording and was tagged as a family and household topic, with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so the page suggested a personal relationship rather than a lodgment arrangement.

value_domain: De-identified MCS supplier identifier
value_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), Section A: Supplier information
variable_description: The organisation that lodged the statement, which is very often an administrator rather than the fund itself, as a de-identified key. The ATO describes the supplier as the party supplying the information, "for example, a tax agent, accountant, superannuation administrator or the provider itself". Grouping rows by this key shows how concentrated super administration is in a handful of firms, and comparing it with the provider key shows which funds run their own back office. The relationship code on the same row says which kind of firm it is.
value_definition: An opaque scrambled identifier, one value per lodging supplier. Where a fund lodges for itself the supplier and the provider are the same organisation and the relationship code is A.
limitation: It says nothing about the member. A change of key between years usually means the fund changed administrator, a back-office event no member ever sees, so it must not be read as the member changing fund. ABS does not document the scrambling, so the key cannot be matched to a named firm.
rationale: The ATO defines what a supplier is on this form and how it differs from the provider, which is what the identifier stands for. The scrambling is a PLIDA treatment that is not published, so the de-identification part of the reading is inference.
evidence_quote: The supplier is a person or organisation supplying the information on the statement (for example, a tax agent, accountant, superannuation administrator or the provider itself).
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Supplier scrambled identifier' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing distinguished the supplier from the provider on the same row.

value_domain: PLIDA person linkage spine identifier (synthetic)
value_source: ABS, Person Linkage Spine
variable_description: The fund member the account belongs to, as the key that carries them across the whole asset. One person has one row per account per year, so the rows under a single key are that person's super history across every fund that lodged for them, which is what makes account counts, contribution totals and balance growth possible. ABS builds the Person Linkage Spine from the Medicare Consumer Directory, DOMINO Centrelink records and Personal Income Tax records and links each dataset to the Spine once, so a contribution can be read against the same person's wages, benefits and Census answers. In this package the values are synthetic: consistent across tables but standing for nobody.
value_definition: An opaque identifier with no internal structure, one value per person, stable across the yearly member contributions tables and across every other dataset linked through the Spine.
limitation: The member is not the contributor. A spouse contribution, an employer contribution and a third-party contribution all sit under the member's key, so this identifier cannot be used to study who is paying. Coverage is also conditional on linkage: an account for a member whose fund did not hold a tax file number may never have reached the Spine and is then unreachable through this key.
rationale: The data item list gives the field as the synthetic member identifier on every member contributions table, and ABS publishes what the Spine is, which datasets build it, what period it covers and why every dataset is linked to it once, which is what determines where this key can and cannot reach.
evidence_quote: The Spine aims to cover all people who were resident in Australia at any point during a given reference period. The current Spine covers January 2006 to June 2025.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's 'Member scrambled identifier' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the key is the PLIDA spine identifier or that a member row does not identify the contributor.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the MCS transferred from reserves, assessable question
value_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement 2013 and later financial years, Section E, question 53
variable_description: Money moved out of a fund reserve into the member's account that the law counts as a concessional contribution. The ATO asks for "the amount that the ITAA 1997 includes as a concessional contribution because an amount was allocated to the member's account from a reserve" and warns that "the amount included by the legislation, and so reported here, may be greater than the amount actually allocated to the member's account". The figure therefore counts against the member's concessional cap even though nobody contributed it and the member may never have asked for it.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount for one member account in one financial year, being the legislated concessional contribution arising from a reserve allocation rather than the cash actually allocated.
limitation: It is not saving in any ordinary sense, so counting it as a contribution overstates member behaviour. It also cannot be netted against the non-assessable reserve column on the same row, which arises under a different rule and counts against a different cap.
rationale: The name expands to the assessable half of the transferred from reserves amounts question on the member contributions statement, and the ATO instruction states both the legal basis and the gap between the amount reported and the amount allocated.
evidence_quote: The amount included by the legislation, and so reported here, may be greater than the amount actually allocated to the member's account.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Transferred from reserve amounts: assessable' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the reported figure can exceed the money that moved.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the MCS transferred from reserves, non-assessable question
value_source: ATO, Super member contributions statement 2013 and later financial years, Section E, question 53
variable_description: Money moved out of a fund reserve into the member's account that the law counts as a non-concessional contribution instead. The ATO defines it as "the amount that the ITAA 1997 treats as a non-concessional contribution because an amount was allocated to the member's account from a reserve and not included as assessable income of the fund". The split from the assessable reserve column beside it is a tax classification, turning on whether the fund had to bring the amount into its own income, not on where the money came from or who benefits.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount for one member account in one financial year, counting against the member's non-concessional contributions cap rather than the concessional cap.
limitation: A figure here signals a fund with reserves to distribute rather than a member doing anything, so it cannot be read as member behaviour. Reserve allocations are concentrated in small funds and defined benefit schemes, which makes the column heavily skewed across providers.
rationale: The name expands to the non-assessable half of the transferred from reserves amounts question, and the ATO instruction gives the legal test that separates it from the assessable half reported in the neighbouring column.
evidence_quote: Provide the amount that the ITAA 1997 treats as a non-concessional contribution because an amount was allocated to the member's account from a reserve and not included as assessable income of the fund.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Transferred from reserve amounts: non-assessable' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained what divides it from the assessable column on the same row.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at the pre-2007 MCS total contributed amount question
value_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 50
variable_description: Everything that went into the member's account for the year on the pre-2007 statement, the control total the component columns build up to. For an ordinary member the ATO defines it as employer contributions plus the post-20 August 1996 termination payment component, allocated surplus, personal contributions and other contributions; for a defined benefit member it is the surchargeable contributions plus personal and other contributions. It is reported by the provider that was holding the contributions for the year, so a fund that transferred the money away before 30 June may not be the one reporting it.
value_definition: A whole-dollar total contribution amount for one member account in one financial year, built from the component amount columns on the same row.
limitation: It does not reconcile in every year. The ATO warned that for the year ended 30 June 2006 the total "may not be the sum of the employer and personal contributed amounts reported" because several component questions became optional, so a gap between the total and its parts is a reporting change rather than an error to fix.
rationale: The name expands to the total contributed amount, the first question in the contributed amounts section of the pre-2007 statement, and the ATO completion guide lists its components separately for accumulation and defined benefit members and flags the year in which the identity breaks.
evidence_quote: For the year ended 30 June 2006, the total contributed amount may not be the sum of the employer and personal contributed amounts reported.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Total contributed amount' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said which columns it totals or that the identity fails in 2005-06.

value_domain: Transferred component of the allocated surplus amount (dollars)
value_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 79
variable_description: The slice of an allocated surplus that left the account when the member's money was transferred out. The ATO asks the fund to "show the amount or part thereof of the allocated surplus amount ... that is contained in the total contributed amount being transferred", so it decomposes the transferred total rather than adding a new contribution. Allocated surplus itself is a fund crediting a member with more than an eligible actuary considers reasonable, which is unusual, so a non-zero value here is rare.
value_definition: A whole-dollar component of the transferred total contributed amount on the same row, populated only where the member has a transfer-out record for the year.
limitation: It cannot be added to the allocated surplus amount for the year without double counting, because it is carved out of that figure. A zero means either that no surplus was allocated or that the transfer carried none of it, and the row does not say which.
rationale: The name expands to the transferred allocated surplus amount, a numbered question in the contributed amounts transfer-out section of the pre-2007 statement, and the ATO guide defines it as a part of the transferred total and defines its parent question separately.
evidence_quote: Show the amount or part thereof of the allocated surplus amount (as reported at question 54 in Section E: Contributed amounts information) that is contained in the total contributed amount being transferred.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Transferred allocated surplus amount' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said it is a decomposition of another column rather than a contribution in its own right.

value_domain: Transferred component of the employer contributed amount, accumulation (dollars)
value_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 76
variable_description: The employer contributions to an accumulation account that went with the money when the member's balance left the fund. Its parent question covers what an accumulation provider reports as taxable contributions made by an employer or another person, together with superannuation guarantee shortfall amounts and Superannuation Holding Accounts amounts the Commissioner paid across. A defined benefit provider leaves the parent question blank, so this transfer column is blank for them too and the defined benefit transfer column beside it carries their figure instead.
value_definition: A whole-dollar component of the transferred total contributed amount, matching the accumulation employer contribution reported at question 51 for the same member and year.
limitation: It is not employer generosity at the point of exit but the year's employer contributions apportioned to a transfer, so a member who left in July shows almost nothing regardless of salary. The destination fund reports the same money for the receiving account, so adding this across funds double counts.
rationale: The name expands to the transferred employer contribution amount for accumulation, a numbered question in the transfer-out section of the pre-2007 statement, and the ATO guide defines both the transfer question and the parent employer contribution question it draws from.
evidence_quote: Show the amount or part thereof of the employer contributed amount (accumulation) (as reported at question 51 in Section E: Contributed amounts information) that is contained in the total contributed amount being transferred.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Transferred employer contribution amount (accumulation)' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said it is a subset of another column or why it is blank for defined benefit funds.

value_domain: Transferred component of the employer contributed amount, defined benefits (dollars)
value_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 77
variable_description: The defined benefit employer amount carried out of the fund when the member's benefit was transferred. The parent figure is not cash: a defined benefit provider reports the surchargeable contributions "that constitute the actuarial value of the benefits that accrued to, and the value of the administration expenses and risk benefits provided in respect of, the member". This column apportions that actuarial value to the transfer out, which is why it can be substantial for a member whose employer never paid a visible contribution.
value_definition: A whole-dollar component of the transferred total contributed amount, matching the defined benefit employer contribution reported at question 52 for the same member and year.
limitation: It is an actuarial construct rather than money that moved, so it cannot be compared with the accumulation transfer column beside it as though the two were the same currency. For the year ended 30 June 2006 the ATO dropped the requirement to calculate notional amounts, so the column can be blank while accrual continued.
rationale: The name expands to the transferred employer contribution amount for defined benefits, a numbered question in the transfer-out section, and the ATO guide defines the parent question as an actuarial value and records the year in which its calculation stopped being required.
evidence_quote: Superannuation (defined benefits) providers must report that part of the total contributed amount that are surchargeable contributions for the financial year that constitute the actuarial value of the benefits that accrued to, and the value of the administration expenses and risk benefits provided in respect of, the member for the financial year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Transferred employer contribution amount (defined benefits)' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the amount is actuarial rather than paid.

value_domain: Transferred component of the other contributed amount (dollars)
value_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 81
variable_description: The residual other contributions that went with the money when the member's balance left the fund. The ATO asks for "the amount or part thereof of the other contributed amount ... that is contained in the total contributed amount being transferred". Because the parent question is defined by exclusion, this column inherits the same fuzziness: government super co-contributions credited during the year travel here rather than in the personal transfer column beside it.
value_definition: A whole-dollar component of the transferred total contributed amount, matching the other contributed amount reported at question 56 for the same member and year.
limitation: What sits inside it varies by fund, so comparing this column between two providers compares classification practice as much as member experience. It is a subset of the transferred total on the same row and cannot be added to it.
rationale: The name expands to the transferred other contributed amount, a numbered question in the transfer-out section of the pre-2007 statement, and the ATO guide defines both it and the residual parent question it draws from.
evidence_quote: Show the amount or part thereof of the other contributed amount (as reported at question 56 in Section E: Contributed amounts information) that is contained in the total contributed amount being transferred.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Transferred other contributed amount' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said it inherits a residual definition from another column.

value_domain: Transferred component of the personal contributed amount (dollars)
value_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 80
variable_description: The member's own contributions that travelled with the balance when it left the fund. The ATO asks for "the amount or part thereof of the personal contributed amount ... that is contained in the total contributed amount being transferred". Because government super co-contribution entitlements were worked out from the personal contribution question, this column decides in practice whether the co-contribution followed the member to the destination fund or was paid to the fund they left.
value_definition: A whole-dollar component of the transferred total contributed amount, matching the personal contributed amount reported at question 55 for the same member and year.
limitation: It does not distinguish deductible from after-tax personal contributions, so it says nothing about the tax position of the money that moved. It also measures only the current year's contributions inside the transfer, not the balance transferred.
rationale: The name expands to the transferred personal contributed amount, a numbered question in the transfer-out section, and the ATO guide defines it against its parent question, which the same guide ties to the co-contribution calculation.
evidence_quote: Show the amount or part thereof of the personal contributed amount (as reported at question 55 in Section E: Contributed amounts information) that is contained in the total contributed amount being transferred.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Transferred personal contributed amount' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said it is a slice of the transferred total rather than a contribution.

value_domain: Transferred component of the post-20 August 1996 ETP amount (dollars)
value_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 78
variable_description: The surchargeable slice of a rolled-in termination payment that went out again when the balance was transferred. The ATO asks for "the amount or part thereof of the post-20 August 1996 component of an employer ETP ... that is contained in the total contributed amount being transferred". Its parent applies only to rollovers made on or after 1 July 1997 and fed a surcharge abolished for contributions from 1 July 2005, so a non-zero value places the row inside a narrow window of years.
value_definition: A whole-dollar component of the transferred total contributed amount, matching the post-20 August 1996 termination payment component reported for the same member and year.
limitation: It is not a redundancy payment. The apportionment formula scales the payment by the share of employment falling after August 1996, so a long-tenured worker with a large payout can show almost nothing here while a recent hire shows the lot.
rationale: The name expands to the transferred post-20 August 1996 employer eligible termination payment component, a numbered question in the transfer-out section, and the ATO guide defines both it and the apportionment formula behind its parent question.
evidence_quote: Show the amount or part thereof of the post-20 August 1996 component of an employer ETP (as reported at question 53 in Section E: Contributed amounts information) that is contained in the total contributed amount being transferred.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's long label, typo included, and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the amount is an apportioned slice of a payment under a repealed surcharge.

value_domain: Transferred total contributed amount (dollars)
value_source: ATO, How to complete the Superannuation member contributions statement (NAT 2603), question 75
variable_description: How much of the year's total contributions left the fund with the member, and the control total for the transfer-out block. The ATO states that it "cannot be greater than total contributed amount shown at question 50", and its components sit in the columns beside it: employer accumulation, employer defined benefit, termination payment component, allocated surplus, personal and other. The block is completed when contributions leave through a lump sum, a pension, an annuity, a departing Australia superannuation payment or a death benefit.
value_definition: A whole-dollar total for one transfer-out record, bounded above by the total contributed amount reported for the same member account and year.
limitation: It measures contributions that moved, not the balance that moved, so a member rolling decades of savings into a new fund can show a small figure. Its presence also does not mean the member left the system: a death benefit, a departing Australia payment and an ordinary rollover all populate it, and this column alone cannot tell them apart.
rationale: The name expands to the transferred total contributed amount, the first question in the contributed amounts transfer-out section of the pre-2007 statement, and the ATO guide gives the ceiling rule, the component questions and the events that trigger the section.
evidence_quote: Please note that the 'Transferred total contributed amount' cannot be greater than total contributed amount shown at question 50 in Section E: Contributed amounts information.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Transferred total contributed amount' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what the transfer block is for or what bounds the figure.
